prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, making the construction of aryl amines a general and practical synthetic operation

statement.case_for: I keep Buchwald and Hartwig as my preferred configuration after reading the full first round. The test I apply is what was new chemically and whether it can be verified in practice. Here the answer is concrete: ligand design (bulky, electron-rich phosphines and biaryl phosphines) turned a substrate-limited C-N bond formation into a general operation, the catalytic cycle was worked out step by step, and more than 25 years of independent use in medicinal and process chemistry can be checked in the literature. Attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist: two independent laboratories, with Kosugi's tin-amide coupling a precursor rather than the general catalytic method. I do not need a mechanism to remain unsettled or a clinical record to arrive before I can state the achievement and its credit in two sentences.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection stands: C-N coupling extends a concept honoured in 2010, and some colleagues will see this as a second prize in the same territory. My choice also has no explicit support from other members in round 1, and I have not found an argument in the exchange that gives me a chemical reason to leave it. I accept that degradation has far broader backing and a more consequential reach for a general audience; if the committee turns to B044 I regard that as a defensible outcome, and my concerns there are about citation scope, not about whether the science is real.

responses.point: Your chair question asks whether PROTACs and molecular glues can be one achievement, and your configuration (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) joins them through the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide-class drugs.
responses.response: I do not think a single citation can honestly state a unifying principle without implying that Handa's work is PROTAC chemistry. Induced proximity is a good organizing idea, but the two strands arrived there from different directions: the PROTAC is a designed bifunctional molecule, while cereblon was identified as the target of a drug already in use and the glue mechanism was understood later. What Handa's work adds chemically is the identification of the protein that thalidomide binds, which is essential but is a target-identification result; the neosubstrate-recruitment explanation came substantially from other laboratories that are not on this shortlist. If the committee goes with B044 I would find Crews and Deshaies alone, as Chabes proposes, more defensible than a trio that implies two discoveries stapled together. On maturity, I agree with you that the absence of an approved PROTAC is not by itself disqualifying, and I would not use it against B044.

responses.point: You pair base editing (Liu alone) with degradation (Crews and Deshaies) as two cases of turning a biological outcome into a defined chemical event usable as a general tool.
responses.response: Your pairing is coherent as a theme, and I take the argument that deaminase chemistry on a Cas-exposed single-stranded window is real chemistry. I still do not think it is stronger than my reading of B019 in round 1: the enabling idea is programmable Cas targeting, already honoured in 2020, and the chemical novelty is the fusion and directed evolution of deaminases. Liu-only credit also sits uneasily with Komor and Gaudelli as co-inventors of the first base editors, and Kondo and Nishida as an independent line of work. If the committee wants two parts, I would sooner see degradation joined with a methodology achievement than with B019, but I accept that is a judgment about chemical novelty on which we differ.

responses.point: You asked whether I see any reason C-N coupling is still more novel than photoredox, and you propose MacMillan, Yoon and Stephenson for B064 with a fallback to Yoon, Stephenson and Nicewicz or Konig if a repeat prize is unacceptable.
responses.response: I do not claim C-N coupling is more novel in concept than photoredox; photoredox opened radical reactivity that two-electron chemistry could not reach. My preference rests on credit and settledness. Buchwald and Hartwig each own a general reaction class with a clear priority record, whereas in photoredox the early reports came from several groups at about the same time. Your own fallback shows how fragile the three-name set is: it works only by choosing among Yoon, Stephenson, MacMillan, Nicewicz, Konig, Melchiorre and Fukuzumi. I keep B064 as a close alternative, but I would want the committee to settle the repeat-recognition question for MacMillan before relying on it.

responses.point: You hold that the induced-proximity mechanism for degradation is established regardless of clinical approval, and you give Handa the third place so that the glue branch is represented.
responses.response: I agree that the mechanism is established and that independent laboratories have reproduced it with several ligases and targets, which is the standard I use for C-N coupling. Our difference is about the third name and how the citation is drafted, not about the science. Handa's cereblon work explains why thalidomide acts as it does, but the committee would have to say clearly that this is the glue half and that the design rule for bifunctional molecules comes from Crews and Deshaies. I would also want the committee to be honest that Ciulli's VHL ligands and structural work on ternary complexes are what made rational degrader design practical, so leaving him outside the three-person cap has a real scientific cost.

uncertainties: Whether a majority sees C-N coupling as distinct enough from the 2010 cross-coupling prize, or whether the Academy would regard it as an overlap.
Whether Kosugi's precursor work should change the laureate pair; I think not, because the general catalytic method and its mechanistic development belong to Buchwald and Hartwig.
Whether B044 can be framed in one citation and with a third name without being unfair to Ciulli or to the cereblon branch, which determines how comfortably I could vote for it as a second choice.
How much weight to give the absence of an approved PROTAC drug; I lean toward not treating it as disqualifying but have no firm basis to say when the Academy would be satisfied.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal. I have no personal or institutional tie to Buchwald, Hartwig, Kosugi or other shortlisted candidates. My Masamune background is in stereocontrolled synthesis, not in cross-coupling or degradation. I share a Lund affiliation with Linke and Sparr; this does not concern any shortlisted candidate and is unchanged from round 1.
